elements.reason: No abstract text is provided in the retrieved evidence that identifies the report as a systematic review.

The retrieved evidence contains methods/results but no abstract text specifying main inclusion and exclusion criteria.

The retrieved evidence describes quality assessment in Methods/Quality Assessment, but there is no abstract text specifying methods used to assess risk of bias.
The retrieved evidence includes analysis/presentation details in Methods/Data Processing, but no abstract text is provided describing methods to present and synthesize results.
No abstract text is provided that reports the total number of included studies and participants and summarizes relevant study characteristics.
The retrieved evidence reports pooled estimates and associations in results, but there is no abstract text presenting results for the main outcomes.
Meta-analysis summary estimate with confidence interval is present in Results text, but no abstract evidence is provided that reports the summary estimate and its confidence/credible interval.
Direction of effect/group favored for comparisons is not shown in retrieved abstract text; the provided effect directions appear only in non-abstract sections.
No abstract text is provided that summarizes important limitations of the included evidence (e.g., risk of bias, inconsistency, imprecision).
No abstract text is provided providing a general interpretation and implications of results.
Funding information ('no specific funding') appears in Methods text, but no abstract text is provided that specifies the primary source of funding for the review.
PROSPERO registration details are present in Methods, but no abstract text is provided that provides the register name and registration number.
The retrieved evidence does not describe the current state of knowledge or identify important uncertainties about SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia.
The retrieved evidence does not explain the importance and need for conducting the review in light of existing knowledge (beyond general background on surgery-related deaths).

Although the methods mention checking PROSPERO to avoid unnecessary duplication, the retrieved evidence does not identify or cite similar prior systematic reviews or explain why the current review is needed relative to them.
This review is about prevalence and predictors (observational associations) rather than an intervention effects question, so a proposed mechanism of action for an intervention is not applicable.
The retrieved evidence indicates the review concerns SSI prevalence and associated factors, not a complex intervention requiring a logic model of intervention components and outcomes.

elements.quote: To determine the pooled prevalence of SSI following cesarean section and its predictors in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: The review objective is explicitly stated as a clear question/objective describing what the review aims to determine (pooled prevalence and predictors of SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia).

elements.quote: To determine the pooled prevalence of SSI following cesarean section and its predictors in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: The objective focuses on pooled prevalence and predictors of surgical site infection, not on planned intervention effects; therefore PICO (or a variant) for intervention comparisons is not applicable based on the available objective statement.

elements.quote: Inclusion. This SRMA included all articles conducted in all regional state of Ethiopia reporting the prevalence/proportion/incidence of SSI after cesarean section and/or associated factors. All observational study designs (case-control and cross-sectional study designs) were included in this SRMA.
elements.reason: Eligibility specifies population/condition (SSI after cesarean), setting (regional state of Ethiopia), outcome type (prevalence/proportion/incidence and/or associated factors), and eligible study designs (case-control and cross-sectional). It does not explicitly specify follow-up requirements.

elements.quote: Both published articles and grey literatures published in English language from January 1 2013 to September 2023.
elements.reason: Report characteristics for eligibility include language (English) and time window (Jan 1 2013 to Sep 2023) and that both published and grey literature were included.
The evidence provided does not describe a distinction between exclusions due to outcomes not being measured versus exclusions due to outcome results not being reported.

elements.quote: Based on the study region, subgroup analyses were done.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports a basis for grouping in synthesis (subgroups by study region) but the evidence does not show that these groups are explicitly specified for each synthesis and linked to the comparisons in the review objectives.

elements.quote: Exclusion. which lack our outcome of interest: SSI following cesarean section and its predictors were excluded from this SRMA. On the other hand, literatures with poor quality as per the criteria of reviewing articles were excluded from this SRMA.
elements.reason: Rationales are provided for excluding studies that lack the outcome of interest and studies judged poor quality, but the evidence does not provide rationales for other notable eligibility restrictions (e.g., the chosen language and date limits).

elements.quote: The electronic literature search was last performed on September 23, 2023.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports the date when the electronic literature search was last performed.

elements.quote: An appropriate and comprehensive search of PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE, Google Scholar, HINARI and Scopus was done since 2013.
elements.reason: Names of bibliographic databases are reported (PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE, Google Scholar, HINARI, Scopus) and a general coverage statement (“since 2013”) is given, but available coverage dates are not specified for each database individually and no search interface/platform details are provided.
No study registers, regulatory databases, or online repositories (other than bibliographic databases) are identified with their names and any date restrictions.

elements.quote: Wehave checked the PROSPERO database https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/displayrecord.php?) to see whether recently published or ongoing projects exist related to the topic
elements.reason: A URL is provided for PROSPERO; however, URLs for other online sources are not reported in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence does not state any organisations or manufacturers contacted to identify studies.
The retrieved evidence does not describe any types of individuals contacted to identify studies.
The retrieved evidence does not specify the types of reference lists examined.
The retrieved evidence does not report any backward/forward citation searching methods (seed reports, citation index/platform, or search date).
The retrieved evidence does not describe any journals or conference proceedings consulted with source names, dates covered, and search methods.

elements.quote: The following search terms were used: '(prevalence) OR (magnitude) OR (proportion) OR (epidemiology) OR (surgical site infection) OR (surgical site) OR (wound infection) AND (cesarean section) OR (cesarean delivery) OR (post cesarean section) AND (determinants) OR (associated factors) OR (risk factors) OR (predictors) AND (Ethiopia)'
elements.reason: The manuscript reports overall search terms and sources searched, but does not provide the complete search strategy as actually run for each database/register/website (e.g., PubMed/MEDLINE/EMBASE/Scopus/CINAHL/Google Scholar/HINARI) with database-specific syntax.

elements.quote: Eligible literatures in English language only were identified. ... An appropriate and comprehensive search of PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE, Google Scholar, HINARI and Scopus was done since 2013.
elements.reason: Search limits (English language only; since 2013) are described, but the evidence provided does not justify these limits by reference to the eligibility criteria.
There is no information in the retrieved evidence about published search approaches/filters being cited or any adaptations.
No natural-language processing or text-analysis tools used to identify or refine search terms are reported in the retrieved evidence.
No tools used to translate search strings between sources are reported in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence does not describe any validation of the search strategy, including the validation process or validation studies.
No peer review of the search strategy (e.g., PRESS) or related process/tool is reported in the retrieved evidence.

The retrieved evidence does not report the final conceptual structure and explorations used to develop the search structure (e.g., only if not based on PICO), and it does not state that such an alternative structure was used.
No explicit reporting of the number of reviewers screening records and full reports at each screening stage in the selection process.
The evidence states independent data extraction by two authors, but it does not explicitly report whether reviewers worked independently during screening of records and full reports.

elements.quote: Any disagreement between reviewers was resolved by the third author (AA). Consensus was declared through critical discussion and evaluation of the articles by all the independent reviewers.
elements.reason: Processes for resolving disagreement are described (third author resolution and consensus via discussion), but the excerpt is framed in the context of data extraction rather than explicitly the screening disagreement process.
No description is provided of processes to obtain or confirm eligibility information with study investigators.
No methods are reported for translating abstracts or full articles for eligibility assessment.
No description is provided of integrating automation tools into the study selection process.
No externally derived classifiers (version/reference), their role, or removal of records before screening is reported.
No internally derived classifiers (including training/validation) are described.
No machine-learning prioritisation tools or screening stopping/prioritisation rules are described.
No information is provided about crowdsourcing platforms or their integration into the selection process.
No description is provided of previously screened datasets used to eliminate records and how they were derived.

elements.quote: Two authors (ES and MA) independently extracted all the important data
elements.reason: States that two authors extracted the data.

elements.quote: Two authors (ES and MA) independently extracted all the important data using standardized data extraction format developed according to 2014 Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Reviewers' manual [24].
elements.reason: Explicitly reports independent data extraction by two authors.

elements.quote: Any disagreement between reviewers was resolved by the third author (AA). Consensus was declared through critical discussion and evaluation of the articles by all the independent reviewers.
elements.reason: Describes how disagreements were resolved and that consensus was reached via discussion/evaluation.
No process is described for obtaining or confirming data from study investigators.

elements.quote: All the datasets were exported to Mendeley reference manager, and then we transferred to the Microsoft Excel spreadsheet to remove duplicate data in the review.
elements.reason: Mentions use of Mendeley and Microsoft Excel for dataset export/duplicate removal, but does not describe automation tools for data collection (including training/validation).
No method is reported for translating articles for data collection.
No software or method is specified for extracting data from figures.

elements.quote: Articles which fulfilled the predetermined criteria were used as a source of data for the final analysis.
elements.reason: Provides a high-level decision rule (predetermined criteria for inclusion in final analysis) but does not clearly describe decision rules for selecting data from multiple reports or resolving inconsistencies in detail.

elements.quote: This SRMA has comprised of two main outcomes. The primary outcome was magnitude of SSI among women underwent cesarean section, which is defined as the proportion of women after cesarean section who fulfills the CDC criteria of surgical site definition within 30 days of post-partum and it could be at least one of the following: ( A superficial incisional , deep incisional or deep/organ SSI) . The secondary outcome was the determinants of SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: Two outcome domains (primary: magnitude of SSI; secondary: determinants) are explicitly stated and the primary outcome is defined.

elements.quote: The primary outcome was magnitude of SSI among women underwent cesarean section, which is defined as the proportion of women after cesarean section who fulfills the CDC criteria of surgical site definition within 30 days of post-partum
elements.reason: A measurement time frame (within 30 days of post-partum) is specified for the primary outcome, but no time frame is provided for the secondary outcome (determinants).
The evidence does not state whether all compatible results within each outcome domain were sought (e.g., all measures/time points/analyses).
No information is provided about selecting results when not all compatible results were sought.
No changes to outcome-domain inclusion, definitions, or importance (with rationales) are reported in the retrieved evidence.
No changes to processes for selecting results within eligible outcome domains (with rationales) are reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: This SRMA has comprised of two main outcomes. The primary outcome was magnitude of SSI among women underwent cesarean section... The secondary outcome was the determinants of SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: The manuscript identifies which outcomes were considered primary vs secondary, but no rationale for prioritising these outcomes is provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The name of the author, sample size, publication year, study region, study design, prevalence/proportion of surgical site infection, and adjusted odds ratio with its 95% CI of the factors associated with SSI.
elements.reason: The review lists several data items that were extracted, but it does not define these variables (e.g., operational definitions for outcomes like “prevalence/proportion of surgical site infection” or for “factors associated with SSI”).
No description of assumptions made about missing or unclear information is provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Two authors (ES and MA) independently extracted all the important data using standardized data extraction format developed according to 2014 Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Reviewers' manual [24].
elements.reason: The standardized data extraction format used to determine which data items to collect is described and linked to the 2014 JBI Reviewers' manual.

elements.quote: we used Newcastle-Ottawa Quality Assessment scale (NOS) adapted for observational studies to assess the quality of each study included in this SRMA [25] (S1 Table).
elements.reason: The tool is specified (Newcastle-Ottawa Quality Assessment scale, NOS) and it is stated as adapted for observational studies, but the specific tool version is not reported.

elements.quote: This quality assessment scale evaluates the literatures in three categories: Selection (4 points) Comparability(2points) and Outcome (3 points)
elements.reason: The domains/categories assessed (Selection, Comparability, Outcome) and their point allocations are reported.
No information is provided about whether an overall risk-of-bias judgement was made and the rules used to derive it.

elements.quote: we used Newcastle-Ottawa Quality Assessment scale (NOS) adapted for observational studies to assess the quality of each study included in this SRMA [25] (S1 Table).
elements.reason: It is stated that NOS was adapted for observational studies, but the specific adaptations (beyond this statement) are not described.
There is no description of any newly developed risk-of-bias tool or public accessibility information.

elements.quote: Two Authors (ES and MA) assessed the quality of each study ... In the case of disagreement between two authors; another third author (AA, WS and BB) were involved and discussed and resolved the disagreement.
elements.reason: The number of reviewers (two authors ES and MA) and the disagreement resolution procedure (a third author(s) involved to discuss and resolve disagreement) are reported.
No process is described for obtaining or confirming risk-of-bias information with study investigators.
No automation tools for risk-of-bias assessment are described.

elements.quote: A random effect model was used to estimate the pooled prevalence of SSI. Adjusted Odds Ratio (OR) with 95% Confidence Interval (CI) was also considered to determine the association of identified variables with SSI.
elements.reason: The effect measures used for outcomes are explicitly stated: pooled prevalence (random-effects model) for SSI magnitude/proportion, and adjusted Odds Ratio (OR) with 95% CI for associations with determinants.
No thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect sizes (and their rationale) are reported in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence does not describe any methods for re-expressing synthesized results using another effect measure.
The retrieved evidence states which effect measures were used, but it does not provide a justification for the choice of effect measure.

elements.quote: Inclusion. This SRMA included all articles conducted in all regional state of Ethiopia reporting the prevalence/proportion/incidence of SSI after cesarean section and/or associated factors. All observational study designs (case-control and cross-sectional study designs) were included in this SRMA. Both published articles and grey literatures published in English language from January 1 2013 to September 2023. Exclusion. which lack our outcome of interest: SSI following cesarean section and its predictors were excluded from this SRMA. On the other hand, literatures with poor quality as per the criteria of reviewing articles were excluded from this SRMA.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes overall inclusion and exclusion criteria for study eligibility, but the evidence does not describe the specific processes used to decide eligibility for each synthesis (e.g., tabulating study characteristics and comparing against planned groups for each synthesis).

elements.quote: All the datasets were exported to Mendeley reference manager, and then we transferred to the Microsoft Excel spreadsheet to remove duplicate data in the review.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes a data preparation step (exporting to Mendeley and using Excel to remove duplicate data), but it does not describe other required preparation methods for presentation/synthesis (e.g., handling missing summary statistics or data conversions).

elements.quote: Therefore we have used the random effect model to resolve the issue of heterogeneity between included studies.
elements.reason: The meta-analysis model (random-effects) and its rationale (to resolve heterogeneity) are explicitly stated.

elements.quote: A random effect model was used to estimate the pooled prevalence of SSI.
elements.reason: The statistical method/model used for the pooled synthesis (random-effects model) is reported.

elements.quote: Cochrane Q-test and I 2 statistics were computed to assess heterogeneity among all the studies included in this SRMA.
elements.reason: The methods used to identify/quantify heterogeneity (Cochran Q-test and I² statistics) are explicitly described.
No between-study variance estimator (e.g., DerSimonian–Laird, REML) for the random-effects meta-analysis is reported in the retrieved evidence.
While 95% confidence intervals are mentioned, the specific method used to calculate the confidence intervals for the random-effects summary effect is not reported in the retrieved evidence.
No additional random-effects implementation details (beyond using a random-effects model) are provided in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence describes frequentist random-effects meta-analysis; no Bayesian meta-analysis is reported, so prior distributions are not applicable.
The retrieved evidence does not describe any approach to account for statistical dependency among multiple estimates from the same study.
No statements are provided about planned syntheses judged impossible or inappropriate, nor reasons for such decisions, in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Based on the study region, subgroup analyses were done. The stability or robustness of the pooled estimates to outliers and the impact of individual studies were assessed using sensitivity analysis.
elements.reason: The manuscript states that subgroup analyses (by study region) and sensitivity analysis were used to explore heterogeneity.

elements.quote: Subgroup analysis was done based on the study region.
elements.reason: The factor for subgroup analysis (study region) is reported, but the evidence does not report the factor levels and expected direction of effect modification for heterogeneity exploration.
The evidence does not specify whether subgroup analyses/heterogeneity exploration used study-level variables, within-study contrasts, or both.

The manuscript reports statistical tests to compare subgroup effects (Q tests for equality of subgroup effects), but the specific method description for how subgroup effects were compared beyond these test statistics is limited in the retrieved evidence.
No informal heterogeneity exploration methods are described for cases where meta-analysis was unsuitable.
The evidence does not identify which heterogeneity analyses were not pre-specified.

elements.quote: The stability or robustness of the pooled estimates to outliers and the impact of individual studies were assessed using sensitivity analysis.
elements.reason: Sensitivity analysis is mentioned conceptually (robustness to outliers and impact of individual studies), but the specific sensitivity analyses performed (e.g., exact procedures/settings) are not described in full detail.
No information is provided on which sensitivity analyses were (or were not) pre-specified.

elements.quote: Funnel plot and Eggers test were done to assess publication bias. The p-value > 0.05 indicated that there was no publication bias.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports statistical methods to assess publication bias (funnel plot/Egger’s test), but it does not explicitly state that these methods were used to assess risk of bias due to missing results in the synthesis (reporting biases from missing study results).
No information is provided about use of an existing assessment tool, its domains/items, or how an overall judgement is derived.
No adaptations to an existing reporting-bias tool are described.
No newly developed reporting-bias tool is described or made publicly accessible.

There is no description of processes for obtaining or confirming relevant information from study investigators.
No automation tools for reporting-bias assessment are mentioned.
No tool/system and version for assessing certainty (or confidence in the body of evidence for outcomes) is reported.
No factors and criteria used to assess certainty/confidence for outcomes are reported.
No decision rules for deriving an overall certainty level (and interpretation of each level) are described.
No review-specific certainty considerations, thresholds, or rationales are reported.
Although NOS is described as adapted for quality assessment, there is no description of adaptations to a certainty-assessment system.

elements.quote: Two Authors (ES and MA) assessed the quality of each study (i.e. methodological quality, sample selection, sample size, comparability and the outcome, and statistical analysis of the study). In the case of disagreement between two authors; another third author (AA, WS and BB) were involved and discussed and resolved the disagreement.
elements.reason: The evidence reports two authors assessing study quality and resolving disagreements, but it does not explicitly state that this is for certainty/confidence assessment (for outcomes).
No process is described for obtaining or confirming relevant information from investigators for certainty assessment.
No automation tools used to support certainty assessment (including training/validation) are reported.
No method for reporting certainty-assessment results (e.g., Summary of Findings tables) is reported.
No intended interpretation or guidance for standard phrases incorporating certainty/confidence is reported.

elements.quote: Atotal of 6334 articles were found by using our search strategies: Google scholar, pub-med, Hinari, EMBASE, Scopus and Medline. After 1398 articles were removed for the reason of duplication, 4932 articles left. Then by reviewing their titles and abstracts, 4800 and 100 articles were removed respectively. Finally 32 full text papers were accessed and evaluated for the predefined inclusion criteria.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports the number of records/articles identified (6334), removed before screening for duplication (1398), screened (4932/4936), and excluded after title/abstract screening (4800 and 100).

elements.quote: Finally 32 full text papers were accessed and evaluated for the predefined inclusion criteria. Thus 13 more articles were excluded for the afore-mentioned reasons.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports that 32 full-text papers were assessed and that 13 were excluded, but it does not report the number of reports sought but not retrieved and does not provide primary exclusion reasons for excluded records at each eligibility stage beyond the general statement.

elements.quote: Eventually, 19 articles were found eligible for inclusion in the final SRMA (Fig 1).
elements.reason: The manuscript reports the number of included studies (19) for the final review.
No information is provided on ongoing studies or associated reports.
No information is provided indicating this is a review update, nor are previous selection results reported.
The reported flow does not distinguish records excluded by humans versus by automation tools.

No studies that might appear eligible but were excluded are cited by name, and no specific reasons for excluding each such study are provided. The evidence only reports aggregate counts (e.g., “13 more articles were excluded”) without identifying excluded studies or linking them to exclusion reasons.

elements.reason: The paper describes a domain/category-based risk-of-bias assessment using NOS (Selection, Comparability, Outcome), but the retrieved evidence does not show that domain-level and overall risk-of-bias judgements are presented in tables or figures for every included study (only that the NOS was used and referenced as “S1 Table”).
The retrieved evidence does not provide justifications for each risk-of-bias judgement for included studies.

elements.quote:
The result of this SRMA showed the overall pooled prevalence of SSI following cesarean section in Ethiopia was 11.13% with a 95% CI: (9.29, 12.97%), which is much higher than the global prevalence of 5.63% [40]. This result is consistent with a study conducted in Rwanda which is 10.9% [14]. However, this was lower than the study conducted in China [15], Jordan [41] and Ekiti state, Nigeria [13] reported 23.3%, 14.4% and 16.01% respectively.

On the contrary, our study finding was much higher than the studies conducted in developed nations: Ireland [42], Poland [5], Estonia [10] and Egypt [43] reported 0.63%, 0.5%, 6.2% and 5.34% respectively.
elements.reason: The discussion explicitly compares the review’s pooled prevalence results with other evidence (global prevalence and studies from Rwanda, China, Jordan, Nigeria, and developed nations) and explains possible reasons for discrepancies.
